title: SD PUC Order — Docket EL26-003: In the Matter of the Application of Black Hills Power, Inc. dba Black Hills Energy for Authority to Increase Rates For its Utility Service in South Dakota (Order Granting Motion for Approval of Procedural Schedule)
text:

ORDER GRANTING MOTION

PROCEDURAL SCHEDULE 
EL26-003 
On February 19, 2026, the South Dakota Public Utilities Commission (Commission) 
received an Application by Black Hills Power, Inc. dba Black Hills Energy (BHP) for approval to 
increase rates for electric service to customers in its South Dakota service territory by 
approximately $50.6 million annually or approximately 25.1 % based on BHP's test year ending 
September 30, 2025. The Company states a typical residential electric customer using 650 kWh 
per month would see an increase of $25.13 per month. The proposed changes may potentially 
affect approximately 75,000 customers in BHP's South Dakota service territory. 
On February 26, 2026, the Commission electronically transmitted notice of the filing and 
the intervention deadline of April 17, 2026, to interested individuals and entities on the 
Commission's PUC Weekly Filing electronic listserv. On April 8, 2026, John D. McKee Sr. was 
granted intervention. On May 13, 2026, Dakota Panel, Fischer Furniture, Inc., Forest Products 
Distrib·utors, Inc., GCC Dacotah, Inc., Monument Health Rapid City Hospital, Inc., Pete Lien & 
Sons, Inc., the South Dakota Science and Technology Authority, and Spearfish Forest Products 
Inc., collectively referred to as the South Dakota Large Customer Group, were each granted 
intervention. On May 11, 2026, Staff filed a Motion for Approval of Procedural Schedule. On May 
18, 2026, BHP filed a Response to Staff's Motion for Procedural Schedule supporting Staff's 
proposed schedule conditioned on a request that a BHP witness be permitted to participate and 
provide testimony virtually. On May 19, 2026, Mr. John D. McKee Sr. filed an Objection to BHP's 
Conditional Acceptance of the Procedural Schedule. 
The Commission has jurisdiction in this matter pursuant to SDCL Chapters 1-26 and 49-
34A and ARSD Chapter 20: 10: 13. 
At its regularly scheduled meeting on May 19, 2026, the Commission considered this 
matter. Staff requested the Commission grant the Motion for Approval of Procedural Schedule. 
Neither BHP or South Dakota Large Customer Group objected to the Staff's Procedural Schedule, 
although BHP noted that BHP did not object, conditioned upon the Commission allowing one of 
its witnesses to appear remotely at the evidentiary hearing. Intervenor John D. McKee Sr. did not 
appear. The Commission voted unanimously to grant the Motion for Approval of Procedural 
Schedule filed on May 11, 2026. The Commission did not act on BHP's request for a witness to 
participate and provide testimony virtually as the request was not timely filed pursuant to ARSD 
20:10:01 :02.05. It is therefore 
ORDERED, that the Motion for Approval of Procedural Schedule is granted. It is further 
ORDERED, that the procedural schedule is established as follows: 
Staff/Intervenor Testimony Due ..................... October 19, 2026 

All Parties' Rebuttal Testimony Due .. .. ............ November 16, 2026 
File Exhibits and Witness List. ....... .... . ... .. .. ... December 1, 2026 
Prehearing Conference .. ..... ......... ... ....... .. ... December 3, 2026 
Evidentiary Hearing .......... ..... .... ... .... ... .... ... . December 8-10, 2026 
It is further 
ORDERED, that responses to discovery are due ten calendar days after service of 
discovery unless a different period is agreed upon by the requesting Party and responding 
Party. It is further 
ORDERED, that prefiled testimony is prerequisite to the offering of testimony at the 
evidentiary hearing and all exhibit and witness lists be prefiled in accordance with the 
procedural schedule.
